title: What a warp does at a branch
summary: Divergence inside a warp, and why the same branch can be free or cost double.

choices.text: Each warp runs only one side of the branch, so the cost is one call per thread, as with no branch at all.
Each thread runs both functions, because the compiler cannot know which side a thread will take.
Every warp holds both even and odd lanes, so each warp runs both sides one after the other: about twice the time of one call.
Odd threads wait at the branch until even threads finish the whole kernel, then run.
